title: UroExact – A Registry Study for the Development of Individualized Treatment Algorithms in Uro-Oncology
summary:
Background: Cancers of the prostate, kidney, bladder, testicles or penis can behave very differently from one person to another. Some grow slowly, others quickly. Some respond well to treatment, others hardly at all. Yet many patients still receive the same treatment, even though they benefit from it to very different degrees. New tests of tumour tissue and blood, and special imaging scans, can help us understand these differences better.

Research question: We want to find out which features of a cancer or of a person predict how well a treatment works, how well it is tolerated and how the disease will develop. In the long term, this should help doctors choose the most suitable treatment for each patient.

Methods: Adults with one of these cancers, or a well-founded suspicion of one, who are treated at TUM Klinikum in Munich can take part. Over many years, we collect the information that arises anyway during normal treatment. This includes the diagnosis, blood values, results of X-ray and other scans, tests on the tumour tissue and its genetic material, the treatments received and their side effects, and how the disease develops.
Taking part does not change the treatment, and there are no extra appointments. Participants also decide separately whether we may study tissue already stored from earlier operations or tissue samples for research. They also decide whether a small extra amount of blood may be taken during blood draws that are happening anyway (no more than 40 millilitres per draw) and whether we may contact them again later.
The data are stored under a number instead of a name and analysed together. Taking part is voluntary and can be stopped at any time without any disadvantage.
conditions: Well-founded suspicion of a urological malignancy (prostate, kidney, upper urinary tract, bladder, testis including extragonadal germ cell tumours, penis) prior to histological confirmation

interventions.name: Patients aged ≥ 18 years with a urological malignancy or a well-founded suspicion of one (in particular prostate, renal cell, urothelial and penile cancer and testicular/germ cell tumours) who present for routine care at TUM Klinikum. There is no intervention; diagnostics and treatment follow clinic

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Age ≥ 18 years
Urological malignancy or well-founded suspicion of one, in particular prostate cancer, renal cell carcinoma, urothelial carcinoma, penile cancer, testicular/germ cell tumour and other urological malignancies
Presentation for routine care at the Department of Urology, TUM Klinikum
Capacity to give informed consent
Information and consent possible in German
Written consent to the collection of treatment data (section 1). The modules on follow-up data, biomaterials and re-contact are optional.
Exclusion criteria:
No consent or refusal to participate
Lack of capacity to consent, e.g. due to severe cognitive impairment
Age < 18 years
Information and consent not possible in German
Pregnancy
